Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a challenging and overwhelming experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time. I'm here to support you and provide a safe and non-judgmental space for you to share your feelings.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may be impacting your well-being during the postpartum period. The EPDS is a brief assessment that screens for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it will help us have a better understanding of your emotional state.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and support you, not to judge. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll be here to support you throughout our conversation.

Let's get started. The first question is: How have you been feeling about yourself and your life in general over the past week? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually enjoy, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope?

.. I don't know, it's just been really tough lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm tired all the time, and it's hard to find the energy to do anything. I used to love taking care of myself, reading, and spending time with my friends, but now it all just feels like too much effort. I mean, I still try to do those things, but it's just not the same. I don't feel like I'm really enjoying them like I used to. And when it comes to taking care of the baby, I feel like I'm just trying to survive each day. I worry all the time about whether I'm doing everything right, if the baby is safe, if I'm feeding her enough... it's just constant. And some days, it feels like it's all just too much for me. I feel sad and overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I even feel like I'm not a good mom, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with. (pausing, getting a bit choked up) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to talk about this stuff.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still try to laugh and find the humor in things, but it's just not as easy as it used to be. I feel like I'm so caught up in worrying about the baby and trying to take care of everything that I don't have the energy to laugh like I used to. Sometimes my husband will try to make a joke or do something silly to make me laugh, and I'll smile, but it doesn't feel as genuine as it used to. It's like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll laugh because I know I should, but it doesn't feel like it's really coming from a happy place. And sometimes, when I do laugh, I'll feel guilty afterwards, like I shouldn't be laughing when I have so much to worry about. It's weird, because I used to be a really happy person, and I loved to laugh, but now it just feels like that's not me anymore. (looking down, frowning slightly)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like another thing to worry about. Like, I'll think about doing something with the baby, or going out with my husband, and instead of feeling excited, I just feel anxious. I'll start thinking about all the things that could go wrong, or how I'll manage to take care of the baby, and it just feels overwhelming. I don't really feel like I'm looking forward to things like I used to. Even simple things, like taking a shower or getting a cup of coffee, feel like chores now. I just feel so tired and drained all the time, and it's hard to muster up the energy to get excited about anything. (sighing) Sometimes I'll think about things I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but then I'll just feel guilty because I don't have the time or energy to do it. It's like, I'm just trying to survive each day, rather than actually enjoying it. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) It's hard to explain, but it just feels like the joy has been sucked out of everything.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Oh, yeah... I do that all the time. I feel like I'm constantly criticizing myself, wondering if I'm doing everything right, if I'm a good enough mom... It's like, no matter what I do, I'm always thinking, "What if I'm messing this up?" or "What if I'm not doing enough?" And if something goes wrong, even if it's just a little thing, I'll beat myself up over it. Like, if the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think, "This is all my fault, I'm a terrible mom." Or if I'm not producing enough milk, I'll think, "I'm failing my baby." It's like, I'm always looking for ways to blame myself, even when it's not rational. My husband will try to tell me that it's okay, that I'm doing a great job, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of guilt and self-doubt. (wiping away a tear) Sometimes I'll even find myself thinking, "If only I had done this or that, things would be better." It's like, I'm constantly second-guessing myself, and it's exhausting. (sighing) I just wish I could be kinder to myself, you know?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something ridiculous, like what if the house catches on fire, or what if someone breaks in. Or I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll start thinking about all the things that could happen to the baby, like SIDS or some other terrible thing. It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I can't shut it off. (taking a deep breath) And it's not just big things, either. I'll worry about little things, like whether the baby is too hot or too cold, or whether I'm feeding her enough. It's like, I'm always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. (rubbing my temples) Sometimes I'll even find myself checking on the baby constantly, just to make sure she's still breathing, or that she's okay. It's exhausting, and it's hard to explain, but it's just this constant feeling of anxiety that's always lurking in the back of my mind. (looking up, tears in my eyes) And the worst part is, I know it's not rational. I know that most of the things I'm worrying about are unlikely to happen, but that doesn't stop me from worrying about them anyway. (sighing) It's like, my brain is just hardwired to worry, and I don't know how to turn it off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath, my voice shaking slightly) Yes... that's happened to me too. There have been times when I've just felt this overwhelming sense of panic, like my heart is racing and I'm going to pass out. It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to something, even though there's no real reason to be scared. Like, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of fear wash over me. My mind will start racing, and I'll think, "What if something happens to me? What if I'm not here for the baby?" (shuddering) It's a really scary feeling, and it's hard to calm myself down when it happens.

(looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes it happens at night, when I'm lying in bed and I can hear the baby stirring in her crib. I'll feel this sudden jolt of fear, and I'll think, "What if something's wrong with her? What if she's not okay?" And I'll get out of bed and go check on her, even though I know she's fine. It's like, my body is just reacting to this perceived threat, even though there's no real reason to be scared.

(taking another deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is just wired to be on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong. And when those feelings of panic come, it's like I'm completely powerless to stop them. (looking up, tears in my eyes) It's a really scary and overwhelming feeling, and it's hard to know how to make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(nodding, feeling a sense of relief that someone finally understands) Oh, yes... all the time. It feels like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, managing the household, trying to be a good partner... it all just feels so overwhelming. Some days, I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart.

(sighing) I feel like I'm constantly playing catch-up, trying to keep up with all the things that need to be done. And no matter how hard I try, I always seem to be one step behind. The laundry is never done, the dishes are always piling up, and the baby is always needing something. It's like, I'm just running on this never-ending treadmill, and I don't know how to get off.

(looking down, feeling a sense of shame) And it's not just the practical things, either. It's the emotional stuff, too. I feel like I'm supposed to be this perfect, happy mom, but the truth is, I'm just struggling to keep my head above water. I feel anxious and overwhelmed all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a functioning adult, but really, I'm just winging it and hoping for the best.

(looking up, tears in my eyes) It's hard to admit, but I feel like I'm just not coping very well. I feel like I'm failing at this whole mom thing, and it's a really scary and overwhelming feeling. (my voice cracks) I just wish someone would tell me that it's okay, that I'm not alone, and that I don't have to do it all by myself.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a sense of recognition) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. It's like, my mind is just racing and I couldn't turn it off, even if I wanted to. I'll lie in bed and think about all the things that could go wrong, or all the things I need to do, and it's just impossible to relax.

(sighing) And it's not just at night, either. I feel like I'm always "on", always waiting for the other shoe to drop. I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or playing with her, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of anxiety wash over me. It's like, my body is just tense all the time, waiting for something to go wrong.

(looking down, feeling a sense of frustration) And it's hard, because I know I need sleep. I know that I need to be rested in order to take care of the baby and be a good mom. But it's just so hard to wind down and relax. I feel like I'm always on edge, always waiting for something to happen.

(shaking my head) And it's not just the lack of sleep, either. It's the quality of sleep, too. I'll fall asleep, but then I'll wake up in the middle of the night and not be able to go back to sleep. Or I'll have these vivid dreams that are just so realistic, and they'll leave me feeling anxious and on edge. It's like, my mind is just not giving me a break, even when I'm asleep.

(looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could sleep, you know? I wish I could just relax and feel like myself again. But it's hard, when you're always feeling like you're walking on eggshells, waiting for something to go wrong.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. I'm just numb, you know? And when I do feel something, it's usually sadness or anxiety. I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying for no reason. It's like, this overwhelming feeling of sadness just washes over me, and I don't know how to make it stop.

(wiping away a tear) And it's not just the big things, either. It's the little things, too. Like, I'll be trying to get the baby to sleep, and she'll just refuse to settle down, and I'll feel this wave of frustration and sadness. Or I'll be trying to make dinner, and I'll just feel so overwhelmed by all the things I need to do, and I'll start crying.

(looking down, feeling a sense of shame) I feel like I'm supposed to be happy, you know? I'm supposed to be this happy, glowing new mom, and I'm just not. I'm sad, and I'm anxious, and I'm overwhelmed. And it's hard, because I feel like I'm failing somehow. I feel like I'm not doing this mom thing right, and that's just making everything worse.

(taking a deep breath) But it's not just me, is it? I mean, I've heard that it's normal to feel this way after having a baby. That it's just hormones and stress and all that. But it's hard to remember that when you're in the middle of it, you know? It's hard to remember that it's not just me, that I'm not alone in this.

(looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish I could feel like myself again, you know? I wish I could feel happy and carefree, like I used to before the baby was born. But it's hard, when you're feeling so sad and overwhelmed all the time.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, feeling a lump form in my throat) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing nothing, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even always about anything specific, it's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration that builds up inside me and then just pours out.

(wiping away a tear) I've been crying a lot at night, too. After the baby goes to sleep, and my husband is watching TV or something, I'll just sit there and cry. It's like, I'm finally alone, and I can finally let my guard down, and all these emotions just come flooding out.

(looking down, feeling a sense of shame) I feel like I'm crying all the time, and it's just so embarrassing. I'll be out in public, or at a family gathering, and I'll just start crying. It's like, I'm trying to hold it together, but I just can't. And then everyone's looking at me, and they're all like, "Oh, are you okay?" And I'm like, "Yeah, I'm fine," but really, I'm not fine. I'm just a mess.

(taking a deep breath) It's hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this strong, capable mom, and crying all the time just doesn't fit with that image. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just so overwhelmed, and I don't know how to make it stop. I don't know how to make the sadness and the frustration go away.

(looking up, feeling a sense of desperation) I just wish someone would tell me that it's okay, that it's normal to feel this way. That it's normal to cry, and to be overwhelmed, and to not have all the answers. Because right now, I just feel like I'm drowning in all these emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, and speaking in a barely audible whisper) Yes... I have had those thoughts. They're scary and overwhelming, and I don't know how to make them go away. It's like, sometimes I feel like I'm just so trapped and alone, and I don't know how to escape. And the thought of harming myself, it's just... it's there. Lurking in the back of my mind, waiting to pounce.

(looks up, tears streaming down my face) I'm so ashamed to admit it. I feel like I'm a terrible person, a terrible mother, for even thinking such things. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just so desperate for a way out. I feel like I'm drowning in all these emotions, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.

(takes a deep breath, trying to calm myself down) It's not like I really want to hurt myself, it's just... it's like my mind is trying to find a way to escape all the pain and the sadness. And sometimes, that thought just pops into my head, and it's like... it's like a little voice, whispering in my ear, telling me that it's the only way out.

(looks down, feeling a sense of shame and guilt) I know it's not true, of course. I know that there are other ways to deal with these feelings, other ways to cope. But in the moment, when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and alone, it's hard to remember that. It's hard to remember that I'm not alone, that there are people who care about me, who want to help me.

(looks up, pleadingly) I just wish someone would help me. I wish someone would tell me that it's okay, that I'm not alone, that I don't have to feel this way. I wish someone would help me find a way to make these thoughts go away, to find a way to cope with all these emotions. I just want to be happy again, to feel like myself again. I want to be a good mother, a good wife, a good person. I just don't know how to get there right now.

The patient is experiencing a range of emotions and symptoms that are concerning for postpartum depression, including persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and crying spells, as well as difficulty sleeping and overwhelming anxiety. The EPDS score of 29 indicates a high risk of depression, and the patient's responses to the screening questions suggest a strong need for support and intervention. 2. Encourage patient to reach out to emergency services or crisis hotline if they experience any further thoughts of self-harm
3. Develop a plan to ensure the patient's safety and well-being, including regular check-ins and follow-up appointments
4. Provide patient with resources and referrals for postpartum depression support groups and counseling services
5. Encourage patient to prioritize self-care and engage in activities that bring them joy and relaxation
